articles.headline: DeMeco Ryans urges Texans to 'dig deep' after 0-2 start
articles.description: Coach DeMeco Ryans challenged his Texans after they fell to 0-2 on Sunday, asking them: If you call yourselves playmakers, where are the plays?
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- Coach DeMeco Ryans challenged his Texans after they fell to 0-2 on Sunday, asking them: If you call yourselves playmakers, where are the plays?

The 20-6 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals dropped the Texans to 0-2 for the third time in four years. The good news for Houston is that the previous two times they made the postseason and won a playoff game in blowout fashion.

Ryans believes the only way the Texans will turn this season around is through their playmakers.

"Are you making those plays to put the Texans in position to win football games," he said Sunday. "That's what it will come down to. Our guys, they played the right way, but you have to execute, have to find a way to get in the end zone. We want to win any game here, we got to get in the end zone, we have to score points. We have to find a way to fix this through our coaches and players. We're all in this together."

Both defeats this season have featured poor performances from one side of the ball.

In a Week 1 loss to the Buffalo Bills, Houston's defense allowed 36 points, its most since a 31-2 defeat to the Ravens on Christmas in 2024. And in Week 2, the Texans' offense scored just six points, its fewest since that same gave vs. Baltimore. 

Houston faced an uphill challenge entering Week 2 with three starters -- Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins, guard Ed Ingram and linebacker Henry To'oto'o - sidelined. Even without Collins, quarterback C.J. Stroud finished with 353 passing yards, as tight end Dalton Schultz finished with 12 catches for 140 yards.

But the former Pro Bowl quarterback wasn't satisfied with his performance.

"Sadly, we've been here before, but I think we just have to hold each other accountable," Stroud said. "We have to get better. There are a lot of things that we need to be doing better if we're going to win. I think we'll have some conversations this week about that and, you know, get some things fixed."

The Texans went 5 for 17 on third downs, and no wideout finished with more than 37 receiving yards. And even though they outgained the Bengals in yards (374-267), the Texans were 0-for-4 both on fourth downs and in the red zone.

Houston also struggled to run the ball as its offensive line didn't create holes for running backs David Montgomery and Woody Marks. They totaled 18 yards on 14 carries, and it was Stroud who finished as the team's leading rusher with 29 yards.

Having to rely on a passing attack on key downs failed. One major reason: Cincinnati's man defense held Stroud to 102 yards on 8 of 20 passing.

Houston, which views itself as a Super Bowl contender, has shown it can recover from 0-2 starts. But how many times can it rely on that?

For now, Ryans won't lean on those experiences, saying, "It's nothing to look back on of what happened in the past."

"We got to go to work. We got to go play good football. That's the bottom line," he said. "The 2026 Texans have to dig deep. All of us have to look down, look deep within ourselves, and see how

articles.headline: Dak Prescott breaks Tony Romo's Cowboys passing TDs record
articles.description: Dak Prescott became the Cowboys' all-time leader in touchdown passes in Sunday's win over the Commanders, surpassing Tony Romo with 249 in his career.
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Dak Prescott stands atop another Dallas Cowboys record.

With a 24-yard pass to receiver CeeDee Lamb in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders, Prescott became the Cowboys' all-time leader in touchdown passes, surpassing Tony Romo with 249 in his career.

Prescott's scoring throw was a slightly underthrown deep ball to Lamb with 3:13 left to play to provide the final margin.

It also gave him four touchdowns on the day for his fifth four-TD game against the Commanders.

Prescott put himself in position to break the record with a 3-yard touchdown pass to Lamb on the Cowboys' first possession of the game. In the second quarter, he hit Jake Ferguson with a simple 9-yard throw with the tight end wide open in the end zone.

He tied the record with his second touchdown of the game to Ferguson in the third quarter, firing a strike from 12 yards to the tight end, who was blanketed by safety Jeremy Reaves.

Asked leading into the game about the possibility of breaking the record , Prescott said, "Blessed, humbled, thankful to have the opportunity to do so. This game has meant so, so much to me. It's always been, since as long as I can remember, peace, getting out there and just playing this game has given me peace and a level of excitement and joy that it's hard to even put into words. And to now put myself in that category, it's humbling, but I expect to play for a long time. And in my mind, I'm just getting started. I've said it before. I think records are meant to be broken when you're playing long enough and that's just this opportunity for me to do this."

A fourth-round draft pick in 2016, Prescott was already the Cowboys' leader in passing yards (36,443 after Sunday), completions (3,232), attempts (4,824), passer rating (98.2) and completion percentage (66.9%).

Romo had 248 touchdown passes from 2006 to 2016 after not throwing a pass in the first three seasons of his career (2003-05).

Prescott has thrown touchdown passes to 39 different players during his career. Lamb has the most touchdown receptions from Prescott with 37. Former receiver Amari Cooper is second with 22. Among current Cowboys, Ferguson has 16, receiver George Pickens has nine and receiver KaVontae Turpin has six.

What's left for Prescott to chase?

Prescott trails Hall of Famers Troy Aikman (94) and Roger Staubach (85) in victories.

However, Prescott has said on numerous occasions that his biggest goal is getting the Cowboys a Super Bowl victory. They have not had one since 1995, when Aikman won his third Lombardi Trophy. Staubach won two Super Bowls in the 1970s.

articles.headline: NFL Week 2 eye-popping stats from Eagles, Pats, Jets, Bears
articles.description: We found six of the coolest advanced stats to come out of Sunday's games -- from third-down completions to matchup route stats.
articles.body:
Week 2 is in the books! A little less exciting than Week 1 if you're a fan of offense -- only 440 points have been scored through Sunday afternoon's games, whereas 702 had been posted by this time last week. If you're a fan of fumbles, be sure to tune in -- there have been 82 fumbles through the first two weeks of the NFL season so far. Though, if you're a fan of fumbles ... consider becoming a fan of something else.

Every Sunday, I'll find several of the coolest advanced stats from the day's NFL action to share with you. Some call them NFL Next Gen Stats. I call them Next Ben Stats -- the data that might not make it on the broadcast but will make you a smarter fan (and laugh a little bit, probably).

Let's start with the statement day from Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts.

Jump to:

Hurts' long conversions 

Bears' scoring regression

Jets like Mitchell on third down 

Gonzalez vs. Metcalf

Saints' bad first-half offense 

Less pressure on Nix

3: How many third-down conversions Jalen Hurts had on third-and-11 or longer in the Eagles' win -- the first such game of his career.

Hurts had nine total third-down conversions -- the most he has had in any game, regular or postseason.

Hurts' best trait has always been his poise and confidence -- never has that been more clearly on display than against the Titans when things at times did not go the Eagles' way. Their opening methodical drive ended in a 90-yard interception return after Hurts was duped on a quality play from safety Amani Hooker. Running back Saquon Barkley and tight end Dallas Goedert both went down with injury for an offense already missing guard Landon Dickerson. The defense started struggling mightily in the second half.

Hurts, armed with as bad of a run game as he has ever had to endure, still lined up on third down and diced 'em up. The Titans' wanted to be a zone team to keep eyes on Hurts -- think Jeffery Simmons' pregame comment of "making Hurts play quarterback." And Hurts did. His comfort with new receiver Dontayvion Wicks (5 catches, 74 yards) is notable, and DeVonta Smith's rise to WR1 was punctuated by an unbelievable catch against the sideline to set up the go-ahead score.

The Eagles are 2-0. It has been far from pretty, but Hurts is willing this team to tough wins in September.

4: How many third-down conversions WR Adonai Mitchell had for Jets -- after having just 10 in his career (34 games) previously.

Mitchell fell out of trust in Indianapolis after his errors cost the Colts' a tight Rams contest in 2025 -- hence the trade to New York shortly after. The Jets have been nothing but enthusiastic about Mitchell's maturity and focus and you saw the fruits of that labor in a strong, if ultimately disappointing showing, against the Packers.

articles.headline: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
articles.description: The Steelers QB, who is entering his 22nd season in the league, is chasing records, and ESPN will be chronicling his "last rodeo."
articles.body:
Entering his 22nd NFL season -- or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" -- the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.

In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots.

"Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

Rodgers also went on to supplant Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in the second quarter of the Thursday night loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025.

That Rodgers is still chasing records in 2026 is somewhat of a surprise after he suggested at times during the 2025 season that he was nearing the end of his career.

"It's the twilight of my career," he said after beating the Minnesota Vikings in Ireland on Oct. 5, 2025. "I used to say five, six, seven years ago, I was on the back nine. But I'm teeing off on 18 right now."

In that win, Rodgers made two more noteworthy entries into the record books: most completions of 50-plus yards and second quarterback in NFL history to throw 60 or more touchdown passes against multiple franchises.

But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that ever-growing list of historic accomplishments.

Maybe it took him a couple of shots to reach the green, or maybe he took his time finding his shot on the fairway. Either way, the 18th hole is in sight, and Rodgers is crouched in front of his ball, squaring up the putt.

"I thought last year might be it," Rodgers said on the first day of training camp. "And then Mike [McCarthy] got hired. And I talked to the wife, and she said you can do one more year. I said, 'We'll see if it works out.' And it kind of all came together."

Among the milestones in reach for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games (as of Week 2 he has appeared in 289), joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), throwing the fourth-most touchdown passes in NFL history (as of Week 2, he has 528) and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes. And after Week 2, he needs 3,318 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards. 

This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo and lines up his putt on the 18th green. Follow along here for the weekly installments.

articles.headline: NFL Week 2: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 2.
articles.body:
In the early window of NFL Week 2 on Sunday, last week's offensive explosion seemed like a thing of the distant past.

Five teams failed to reach double-digits points, including both the Bears and Vikings at a rainy Soldier Field. The Panthers forced five turnovers against the Falcons, while the Patriots cemented their win over the Steelers with a fumble return for a touchdown. The highest-scoring matchup of the early window (44 points) came between the Titans and Eagles, which ended on a game-winning touchdown grab by Philly's Darius Cooper.

The scoring picked up in the late window Sunday, as the Cowboys and Commanders combined for 57 points. However, Washington lost QB Jayden Daniels to an elbow injury in the third quarter -- hours after Chicago lost QB Caleb Williams to a right hamstring injury. Meanwhile, the 49ers dominated the Dolphins in their first game back from Melbourne, Australia. And the Seahawks won their second straight game with backup quarterback Drew Lock.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

Jump to:

WSH-DAL | LV-LAC

SEA-ARI | MIA-SF

JAX-DEN | CLE-TB | PHI-TEN

GB-NYJ | CIN-HOU | MIN-CHI

NO-BAL | CAR-ATL | PIT-NE

Catch up on Thursday's game:

DET-BUF

Dallas 37, Washington 20

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Cowboys

Are the Cowboys going to need QB Dak Prescott to outscore teams again this season? It looks that way. Prescott broke the Cowboys' record for touchdown passes in a career with four Sunday, eclipsing Tony Romo. But Prescott needed to be everything for Dallas, completing better than 80% of his passes, throwing the four scores and running for 26 yards. The defense had issues again, losing safety P.J. Locke (foot) and corner Cobie Durant (hamstring) in the first half. They continue to struggle on third down, contain a running quarterback and turn pressures into sacks. Washington had three chances for touchdowns wiped out, but Prescott bailed them out ... again.

Trend to watch: The Cowboys want to be a team that relies on the running game to get things going. Through two games, that has not happened. A week after running 18 times for 69 yards against the Giants, the Cowboys followed with 66 yards on 21 carries. No Cowboys running back has a rush of more than 9 yards. The Cowboys miss Pro Bowl left guard Tyler Smith, who will be out for at least the next two games because of thumb surgery, but they shouldn't miss him this much. -- Todd Archer

articles.headline: Michael Carrick keen to find Man United positives, but there aren't many right now
articles.description: This is Man United's worst start in a Premier League season in 12 years. Is there any reason to believe a turnaround is ahead?
articles.headlineJa: マイケル・キャリック、マンUのポジティブな面を見出そうとするも現在は好材料が乏しい状況
articles.descriptionJa: これはマンチェスター・ユナイテッドにとって過去12年間で最悪のプレミアリーグ開幕スタートとなった。巻き返しを信じられる理由は何かあるのだろうか？
articles.body:
LONDON -- For Michael Carrick, the international break won't feel like much of a break at all.

The games will stop, but after Manchester United's 1-1 draw with Fulham on Sunday, the spotlight and the scrutiny will remain. It's going to be a long three weeks for United's coach.

It could have been even worse. Matheus Cunha's 89th-minute equalizer prevented a first defeat at Craven Cottage in 17 years and stopped the pressure on Carrick ramping up to another level.

After back-to-back home defeats to Manchester City and Brighton, three consecutive losses would have left United's decision-makers with some thinking to do while the players jet off to join their national teams.

As it is, a point at Fulham will at least stop the bleeding -- there's not much to shout about. Five points from five games is United's worst start to a Premier League season for more than a decade. And that's after a run of fixtures that appeared on paper to be relatively manageable.

"It's not been ideal," Carrick admitted. "I know we can do better, we need to do better at certain things. But at the same time, I'm not despondent and down because I think we're showing some good signs as well.

"I'm not playing it down. We wanted more points from it."

Though Carrick was keen to find the positives, the most damning part of the day was perhaps the assessment of his former United teammate Gary Neville. The pair played together at Old Trafford for four years, but when Fulham went ahead midway through the second half, Neville did not hold back.

"I've watched Manchester United since the age of 5," he said. "That's the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen them play."

Given some of the disastrous displays over the past decade, it was quite a statement. Neville's outburst -- during which he branded parts of the performance as "pathetic" -- was prompted by a calamitous Fulham goal.

Kobbie Mainoo's pass into midfield was telegraphed by Calvin Bassey, who was too strong for Cunha. Then the Fulham defender was allowed to advance unchallenged into the penalty area before firing a tame shot at Senne Lammens.

But when things aren't going well, even the most innocuous situations can turn into something else. This time, Bassey's shot hit Lammens before rebounding back toward the goal off Lisandro Martínez.

A scrambling Lammens chose to use his feet rather than his hands to stop the ball and succeeded only in booting it into the net. It was either bad luck or symptomatic of a United team struggling with the confidence to make decisive decisions.

Self-belief, or lack of it, is not the only issue for Carrick to address. There's a feeling among some fans that United have not looked fit enough during the early part of the season.

Running stats aren't everything, but at the end of the 90 minutes, Fulham's players had covered an extra 6 kilometers more than United's players. There were certainly times during the game when it appeared obvious that the home side was quicker, faster and sharper.

Cunh

articles.headline: NFL betting buzz: Most popular survivor pick loses for second week in a row with Bucs loss
articles.description: With 27% of ESPN survivor picks and 6,601 entries in Circa Survivor, the Bucs lost at home to the Browns.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in sports has additional context when viewed from a sports betting perspective. From season-changing injuries to record-setting moments and so much more, the sports news cycle will constantly and significantly affect the sports betting industry.

Our NFL betting buzz file, with contributions from David Purdum, Doug Greenberg and others, aims to provide fans a look at the sports betting stories that are driving the conversation throughout each week of the season. 

Key links: NFL futures | Awards odds | Sports betting home | DraftKings 

Sept. 20: Most popular survivor pick loses for second week in a row

By David Purdum

The most popular pick in ESPN.com survivor contests lost for a second straight week.

In Week 1, it was the Los Angeles Chargers, who were upended by the Arizona Cardinals. On Sunday, it was the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as they fell to the Cleveland Browns.

The Chargers were picked in 21% of ESPN entries last week. The Bucs were backed by 27% this week.

In the high-stakes Circa Survivor contest ($1,000 buy-in, $25 million prize pool), 6,601 entries backed the Bucs in Week 2. Only the San Francisco 49ers (versus the Miami Dolphins) were more popular.

The 49ers took care of their business while the Buccaneers did not and lost to the Browns 24-19 at home in a game that featured a lengthy weather delay.

If it provides any solace for Tampa Bay supporters, 42 entries in the Circa contest failed to submit their picks by the deadline. Those entries are now worth the same as the 6,601 that had the Buccaneers.

Tampa Bay, an 8.5-point favorite, failed to cover the spread in its 11th straight game, tied for the longest such streak in the Super Bowl era, according to ESPN Research.

Ahead of the primetime game, Tampa Bay was one of five favorites that lost outright Sunday, joining the Baltimore Ravens, Minnesota Vikings, Cincinnati Bengals and Chargers.

Sept. 13: Circa Survivor kicks off with $25 million grand prize, Jaguars lead Week 1 picks

By Doug Greenberg

The Circa Sports pro football contests are locked in for the 2026 season with a total of $38.7 million on the line. 

Circa Survivor will begin the season with a record 25,017 entries, making a winner-take-all $25,017,000 prize pool. The contest exceeded its guarantee of $20 million with four days remaining before registration closed.

Grandissimo, Circa's $100,000-per-entry survivor contest, also easily met its $4 million guarantee and ended up with a record 77 entries vying for a $7.7 million prize pool. The casino's traditional $100,000-per-entry handicapping contest, Circa Million, did not meet its $6 million guarantee and ended up with 5,790 entries, creating an overlay of $210,000.
